title: Exercise model — Resalat E1 pathway with simulator extensions

caption.scope: The contraction pathway adapts the E1 equation from Resalat et al. (PLOS ONE 15:e0237511, 2020): normalized heart-rate excess is filtered with a 5-minute time constant and enters Q2 once as β·E1. Exercise-specific hepatic output, delayed insulin sensitivity, muscle-glycogen turnover and pulseFactor are explicit simulator extensions calibrated or constrained against exercise literature.

variables.definition: selected activity profile and intensity; supplies independent parameters for contraction uptake, hepatic drive, delayed sensitivity and glycogen use
current heart rate in beats per minute; approaches the activity-specific target gradually
dimensionless contraction-response state; dE1/dt = (exerciseInput − E1) / 5 min
bounded exercise-specific hepatic-output state; decays after exercise with a 30-minute half-life
continuous delayed insulin-sensitivity components with independent activity-specific scales and 15-minute, 4-hour and 18-hour decay half-lives
intracellular bookkeeping pool used during exercise and replenished afterward without an additional plasma-glucose drain
heart-rate-dependent multiplier for rapid and basal subcutaneous insulin absorption
peripheral glucose pool in mmol; receives the contraction-mediated drain
rapid and basal two-stage subcutaneous insulin depots
muscle insulin-action channels whose EC50 is shifted by the delayed sensitivity response; hepatic x3 is unchanged
insulin-independent contraction-mediated glucose uptake applied once in the Q2 equation
hepatic glucose output generated by exerciseHepaticDrive × liver-glycogen availability
activity-specific scale for muscle-glycogen consumption only
rapid and basal insulin appearance rates accelerated by pulseFactor
